title: Sasquatch Resources reports C$131,250 Echo purchase
excerpt: Sasquatch Resources issued 1.25 million shares for Echo on Vancouver Island, with a 2 per cent royalty and six claim applications still pending.
content:
Sasquatch Resources Corp. CNSXSASQ said on Monday it has completed the Echo property acquisition for C$131,250 in shares. The purchase adds eight Vancouver Island claims to its portfolio, subject to a 2 per cent net smelter return royalty.

The CSE issuer page showed shares unchanged at C$0.135, with its latest trade stamped Nov. 11 at 3:59 p.m. EST, before Monday's announcement.

The deal issued 1.25 million shares rather than paying cash to the sellers. For scale, those shares equal about 2.4 per cent of the 52,350,429 shares the CSE issuer page listed as outstanding on Nov. 16.

The acquisition also brings a surface showing where a 19-metre channel sample taken in 2026 included 3.8 metres grading 100 grams per tonne gold. The release gives no dated exploration program or Echo-specific funding allocation.

Echo is near Cowichan Lake in British Columbia. Two granted claims cover 85 hectares, while six applications cover another 362 hectares, so most of the acquired package remains subject to claim grants.

Sasquatch issued the consideration shares at C$0.105 each under its Nov. 5 agreement with Justin Deveault, Andrew Clarke and Rory Munroe. The sellers received the royalty alongside the shares.

Deveault is a director, making the purchase a related party transaction. Sasquatch's Nov. 9 agreement announcement said he abstained from board approval and the transaction qualified for exemptions from formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements.

The surface result came from five consecutive chip-channel samples taken with a chisel and rock hammer. Sasquatch said true mineralization widths remain unknown; the sampled surface length does not establish a drill intercept or an underground extension.

Four historical drill holes started away from the showing returned poor results, according to Monday's release. Sasquatch says their orientation and depth may not have adequately tested the zone, whose extent remains unknown. The company has not verified the historical sampling figures.

"The showing appears to contain significant grades for gold, over significant distances and all right at surface, off a logging road only minutes from paved road access to the Cowichan Valley," chief executive Peter Smith said.

Sasquatch focuses on assessing mineralized waste rock at former mines and logging-road sites in British Columbia. Its existing portfolio includes Blue Grouse, another prospect near Cowichan Lake.

The company raised C$671,000 on Aug. 27, including C$227,500 in flow-through proceeds designated for eligible Canadian exploration expenses. That financing announcement did not assign the exploration proceeds to Echo.

The four-month resale hold on the acquisition shares expires March 17, 2027.
